name: Marko Marulić
credit: Imagined portrait of Marko Marulić (no authentic likeness survives), printed in Ljetopis društva hrvatskih književnika, 1903 · Public domain (Wikimedia Commons)
bio: Marko Marulić (1450–1524) was a Split humanist, jurist and devout Christian writer who composed in Latin, Italian and Croatian. His Latin treatise on the good life, De institutione bene vivendi, was widely read across Europe, while his work in the vernacular has earned him the name of the father of Croatian literature.

His Judita, written in 1501 and first printed in Venice in 1521, retells the biblical story of the widow who beheads the Assyrian general Holofernes. Composed in the Čakavian speech of Split in some 2,126 rhymed twelve-syllable lines, it is regarded as the first epic poem in Croatian.
